Create a new endpoint

Custom Mapper Required

Search API endpoints require a custom mapper to translate your API's response format into Quepid's expected format.

To set up a Search API endpoint:

  1. Use the Mapper Wizard to create your custom mapper code
  2. Return here and select your new endpoint from "Use an existing Search Endpoint" above

A "Static" (or "Offline") search endpoint is a great way to gather human judgements and leverage Quepid's existing evaluation tools without requiring a live connection to a search engine.

Static Dataset

Create the CSV file and upload it here. Under the covers we use the Snapshot CSV format, so you can export a snapshot from Quepid and then upload it here to create a Static search endpoint.

The CSV file should have the headers: Query Text,Doc ID,Doc Position. Then, all the document fields you want displayed follow as columns with the header being the name of the field. 
Query Text,Doc ID,Doc Position, MovieTitle
star wars,527641,1, Star Wars
star wars,9426,2, Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back
star wars,1921,3, Star Wars: Return of the Jedi
Please note that the additional columns that a Snapshot export file contains are ignored when you import them here.

Enter a test query to validate the endpoint works.

Test query is required to validate the endpoint.

Modify your query structure to include #$query## where the search text should be substituted. Quepid will replace #$query## with each query you add.

Query pattern is required.

Your query pattern should include #$query## so Quepid can substitute the search text.

  • Quick fix: check Proxy requests through Quepid above so Quepid's server talks to Elasticsearch instead of your browser. No cluster changes required.
  • Or configure CORS on Elasticsearch to allow Quepid's domain if your team prefers direct browser access.
  • Can you open the URL directly in a new tab? If yes but Quepid still fails, check the browser console for CORS errors.
  • Does your Elasticsearch accept HTTP POST requests?
  • Do you need an API Key? If so, set one up in Custom Headers above.
  • Use the browser Network Inspector to see the actual request.

  • Quick fix: check Proxy requests through Quepid above so Quepid's server talks to OpenSearch instead of your browser. No cluster changes required.
  • Or configure CORS on OpenSearch to allow Quepid's domain if your team prefers direct browser access.
  • Can you open the URL directly in a new tab? If yes but Quepid still fails, check the browser console for CORS errors.
  • Does your OpenSearch accept HTTP POST requests?
  • Use the browser Network Inspector to see the actual request.
  • See the Troubleshooting OpenSearch and Quepid wiki page for more help!
  • Quick fix: check Proxy requests through Quepid above so Quepid's server talks to Solr instead of your browser. No Solr configuration changes required.
  • Do you see any errors when you visit your Solr URL directly? If Solr responds but Quepid still fails, check the browser console for CORS or mixed-content errors.
  • You may need to configure the JSON wt=json to be application/javascript to work with Quepid. You can do this via the below curl command: 
    curl -k -X POST -H 'Content-type:application/json' -d '{
  "create-queryresponsewriter": {
    "name": "json",
    "class": "solr.JSONResponseWriter",
    "content-type": "application/javascript; charset=UTF-8"
  }
}'
    If you get an error message back, change create-queryresponsewriter to update-queryresponsewriter and re-run.
  • If Solr responds, check if you have an ad blocker blocking your queries.
  • Chrome does not accept self signed certificates on Solr, try Firefox.
  • Chrome does not allow basic auth to Solr, try Firefox.
  • Use the browser Network Inspector to see the actual request.
  • See the Troubleshooting Solr and Quepid wiki page for more help!
